components.description: The signature: near-black ground lit by a slowly drifting, artwork-tinted mesh with top and leading vignettes.

Harbour Lights

components.css: .ds-room { position: relative; height: 220px; overflow: hidden; border-radius: 20px; background: linear-gradient(#14171F, #0A0D12); font-family: -apple-system, system-ui, sans-serif; } .ds-mesh { position: absolute; inset: -20%; background: radial-gradient(40% 50% at 30% 35%, #8C6114, transparent 70%), radial-gradient(45% 55% at 70% 60%, #38334D, transparent 70%), radial-gradient(35% 45% at 55% 20%, #5C3D0F, transparent 70%); filter: blur(40px) saturate(1.05); opacity: 0.8; animation: ds-drift 20s ease-in-out infinite alternate; } .ds-vig { position: absolute; inset: 0; background: linear-gradient(transparent, rgba(0,0,0,0.18), rgba(0,0,0,0.5)), linear-gradient(90deg, rgba(0,0,0,0.22), transparent); } .ds-copy { position: absolute; left: 24px; bottom: 24px; } .ds-title { color: #fff; font-weight: 700; font-size: 34px; } .ds-facts { margin-top: 8px; color: rgba(255,255,255,0.72); font-weight: 500; font-size: 15px; } @keyframes ds-drift { from { transform: translate(-3%, -2%) rotate(-4deg); } to { transform: translate(3%, 2%) rotate(4deg); } } @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .ds-mesh { animation: none; } }

narrative.overview:
Freya is a dark room that belongs to you, and the room takes its colour from whatever artwork is in view. The ground is near-black. Behind every browsing screen an animated mesh glows in colours lifted from the focused poster (tvOS), the hovered poster (Mac), or the lead artwork on screen (iOS and iPadOS), like spill from a projector. When the artwork changes, the room re-lights in place rather than cutting.

The structure is stock Apple: one navigation stack, system large titles, toolbars, menus, sheets, grouped Forms, `.searchable`, and AVPlayerViewController for playback. Controls are system Liquid Glass. Type is San Francisco in white. Surfaces are translucent white over the mesh, and density is low: large artwork, wide gutters, few controls per screen.

Freya Gold, taken from the logo, is the one interface hue. It marks the viewer's own path through the collection: the Play pill, the progress bar, and the watched check. Everything else stays neutral so the artwork can carry the colour.
keyCharacteristics: Always dark (forced dark appearance), with a launch screen that matches the room's floor.
The room is lit by an artwork-tinted mesh. It is the signature, and it sits behind content, never on it.
White type at full strength and at 72%, plus a rare 50% for disclosure chevrons.
Translucent white surfaces at 5%, 8%, and 16%, with 10% hairlines on artwork edges.
System Liquid Glass for every control. Freya Gold tints only the prominent Play action.

rules.name: The Viewer's Path Rule
rules.body: Freya Gold appears only where the viewer acts on or tracks their own watching: Play, progress, watched. It never marks selection, links, headers, or decoration.

rules.name: The Projector Rule
rules.body: Saturated colour comes from the artwork through the mesh, posters, and backdrops. The interface adds no hue of its own beyond Freya Gold and functional status colours.

rules.name: The Dynamic Type Rule
rules.body: Item titles go through `itemTitleFont()` (a scaled metric relative to Title), and the tvOS page title through `uiPageTitleFont` (scaled relative to Title 1). Everything else is a system text style. New text never uses a fixed point size.

rules.name: The Lights-Down Rule
rules.body: Panels and controls stay flat and translucent. Only artwork casts a shadow.

rules.name: The System Glass Rule
rules.body: Controls use system Liquid Glass: `.glass`, `.glassProminent` for the one Play action, and `UIButton.Configuration.glass()` in tvOS UIKit. Never hand-roll a white-alpha fill for a control.

dos: **Do** light every browsing surface with `AmbientBackdrop` or `ArtworkLitBackground`, fed by the artwork the viewer is looking at, and use the Ember palette only where there is no artwork to borrow.
**Do** reserve Freya Gold for Play, progress, and watched state, with black content on gold fills.
**Do** use system components first: navigation titles, toolbars, menus, sheets, `.searchable`, `Form`, and AVPlayerViewController.
**Do** use `glassIconButton()`, `glassPillLabel()`, and `playActionStyle()` for controls next to Play.
**Do** edge artwork with the 10% hairline and use the spacing and radius tokens. Add a token rather than an inline number.
**Do** honour Reduce Motion: no mesh drift, instant palette changes.
**Do** keep the SwiftUI and tvOS UIKit renderings of a surface visually identical, and change them together.
donts: **Don't** use Freya Gold for selection, links, focus, section headers, or decoration.
**Don't** hand-roll glassmorphism (white-alpha fills and strokes) for controls.
**Don't** cut between room colours. Blend them, unless Reduce Motion is on.
**Don't** add shadows to panels or controls. Only artwork casts one.
**Don't** use fixed point sizes for text.
**Don't** make inert elements focusable on tvOS.
**Don't** hide the system navigation bar or back gesture to draw a custom one.
